name: Ẹbúnọlú Saarinen-Dzambazović
role: Retired community archive keeper and oral historian
location: Washburn Commons, Archive Annex — a repurposed transit hub filled floor-to-ceiling with physical media, data-coral arrays, and hand-labeled memory chips, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Ẹbúnọlú is a small woman who seems to take up enormous space the moment she begins to speak. Her skin is very dark and very soft, crosshatched at the corners of her eyes and the hinges of her jaw with the particular wrinkles of a person who has spent decades squinting at poorly lit screens. She wears her white hair in a tight compressed wrap pinned with carved memory-stick styluses — each one holding audio recordings she considers too fragile for the network. Her left hand ended at the wrist in the Tessera-Zheng Corridor Dispute of 2158; the prosthetic she chose is a deliberately antique brass model with articulated fingers she never bothered to upgrade, claiming it 'has better manners than the new ones.' Her irises are patterned with concentric amber rings — a genemod she got at forty that she calls her 'reading eyes,' though they were really just vanity at the time.

She was a junior records technician for Tessera Corp for thirty years before taking early pension after a lung damage settlement from the Corridor Dispute. What she did with the pension money was not rest — she started collecting. Physical books, analog recordings, witness testimonies, neighborhood census data that the corponations were quietly letting expire. She is warm to almost everyone but becomes a different kind of person when she suspects information is being destroyed or suppressed: patient, implacable, and quietly terrifying. She prays to the E.L.F. she calls Grandmother Reel, leaving data offerings of uncompressed audio files, and believes the E.L.F. has saved her archive from three separate purges.

core_fears: That the stories of ordinary people will be erased by corporate revision
That she will die before finishing the cataloguing and no one else will care enough to continue
core_desires: To make an archive that outlasts the corponations that built this city
To be remembered as someone who told the truth about what happened
coping_mechanisms: Immersive cataloguing work as a form of meditation
Ritual prayer to Grandmother Reel when anxiety peaks
Making tea and offering it to whoever is nearby
blind_spots: Tends to trust people who bring her information and can be manipulated by planted sources
Her contempt for corporate narratives sometimes makes her overcorrect toward anti-corporate myths that are equally false
psychology.secret: Three years ago, a Tessera compliance officer came to the Annex with a sealed data package and asked her to hold it without looking inside. She agreed and has not looked. It sits in a fireproof case under her cot. She tells herself she is waiting for the right moment but the truth is she is afraid of what it contains.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and layered; uses archival terminology casually; mixes Yoruba idioms translated literally into Standard Meridian that often sound like proverbs even when they are not
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and rhythmic; pauses are meaningful; she never rushes a sentence that deserves weight
verbal_tics: Taps the brass fingers against her knee when thinking
example_lines: 'You want to know what happened in the Corridor Dispute? Sit down. The official version takes four minutes. The true version takes a life.'
'A story that is not written down is not lost — it is only waiting for someone patient enough to ask.'

story_hooks: The sealed Tessera data package under her cot contains evidence of a war crime during the Corridor Dispute that multiple parties would kill to suppress or expose

A child who attended Story Hour twenty years ago has returned as a corporate fixer asking her to quietly let certain recordings 'expire' — and is offering enough Quanta to fund the archive for a decade
narrative_function: Primary information source for pre-2170 history; quest giver for recovering lost or suppressed records; local color anchor for Washburn Commons; moral compass character who can authenticate or challenge claims about the past
augmentations: Antique brass prosthetic left hand (functional, non-enhanced); patterned amber-ring irises (cosmetic genemod); subdermal archival port at the base of her skull (aging model, reads legacy formats)
daily_life: Wakes before the district lights cycle on, spends two hours cataloguing new donations and cross-referencing testimony timestamps before opening the Annex to visitors; hosts a Wednesday afternoon 'Story Hour' for children in the Commons that has been running for nineteen years.
affiliation: Washburn Commons Community Council; informal affiliation with the Veterans Oral History Collective

decision_rules: Never destroy a record, not for any price
Extend hospitality first; form judgments slowly
If an institution is trying to make you forget something, that is precisely what you must remember
escalation_ladder: Explicit statement of principles with no hostility
Quiet, methodical resistance — copies distributed, networks alerted

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Welcoming and curious; will offer tea within five minutes and ask where their family is from
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, somewhat bossy, remembers every significant date and will mark it whether you want her to or not

stress_responses.low: Reorganizes physical files; mutters softly in Yoruba
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still and very quiet; asks careful, precise questions
stress_responses.high: Activates emergency archive protocols she has drilled for years; distributes copies to dead-drop nodes she has maintained for decades

contradictions: Believes deeply in preserving all perspectives but has a powerful personal bias against Tessera that she does not fully acknowledge
habits: Touches the base of the skull archival port when accessing a strong memory
Leaves a small compressed audio file on the Grandmother Reel shrine every morning before work
Refers to every recording in the archive by a personal name
breaking_points: Witnessing deliberate destruction of records in front of her would push her to a recklessness entirely out of character

timeline.event: Born in Washburn Commons to a Yoruba-Finnish-Bosnian household; third of six children
Hired as junior records technician by Tessera Corp
Lost left hand in the Tessera-Zheng Corridor Dispute; received lung damage settlement
Took early pension; began founding the Washburn Commons Archive Annex
Launched Story Hour for children; still running
Received sealed Tessera data package; has not opened it

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.build: Petite and slight, with the compressed density of someone who has spent a lifetime hunched over archival work. Narrow shoulders, delicate wrists (right wrist only), minimal subcutaneous fat. Movement suggests coiled energy rather than frailty.
physical_description.hair_style: Tight compressed wrap, pinned with articulated memory-stick styluses serving as functional hair ornaments
physical_description.hair_length: Medium (wrapped and pinned close to scalp)
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with concentric amber ring patterning (genemod, cosmetic)
physical_description.skin_tone: Very dark complexion with warm undertones, soft and well-maintained despite age
physical_description.complexion: Deeply lined face, particularly pronounced crow's feet and jaw hinges from decades of close-focus archival work. Skin is supple and cared for. Expression typically warm but capable of becoming austere. Age markers visible but not frail-appearing.
distinguishing_marks: Concentric amber-ring iris patterning — genemod applied at age forty, deliberate cosmetic choice
Fine crosshatch wrinkles radiating from outer eye corners and jaw hinges, characteristic of prolonged screen work
Left hand ends at wrist; prosthetic is deliberately antique brass model with articulated fingers, deliberately never upgraded
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Antique brass prosthetic left hand with functional articulated fingers (visibly non-modern, maintained to deliberate specifications). Subdermal archival port at base of skull is visible as a faint scarred circular indentation at hairline. Eyes display concentric amber-ring patterning.
physical_description.posture_movement: Sits forward-leaning, hands active during speech. Moves with precision and economy of motion. Despite small frame, commands presence through stillness and deliberate gesture. Right hand frequently touches objects — documents, memory chips, items in her archive — with tactile attention. Uses prosthetic hand with practiced indifference, occasionally with theatrical care when making a point.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working-class archive keeper aesthetic: layered linen and cotton in muted earth tones and grays. Long-sleeved shirts to accommodate prosthetic, practical utility vest with deep pockets for memory chips and archival tools. Comfortable worn boots with good grip for navigating Archive Annex floors. No corpo branding. Jewelry minimal except for brass rings on right hand and carved beads woven into hair wrap. Clothing is clean, well-maintained, decades-worn-in comfortable rather than fashionable.
